import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 100

**Verbatim statement (WOWII #100, status O):**
> If G is a simple connected graph, then α(G) ≤ CEIL[(maximum of λ(v) + 0.5*length(Ḡ))/2]

**Source:** http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj100

The WOWII HTML uses `length(Ḡ)` (the bar denotes graph complement); the
extracted JSON in our private repo previously dropped the overline. The
formal statement below uses the Euclidean norm of the degree sequence of `Gᶜ`.

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

## Definition of graph length

The WOWII definitions popup defines `length(H)` as the square root of the sum
of the squares of the vertex degrees. This is `degreeL2Norm H` in Lean.
Combined with the overline above, the inequality reads:
  `α(G) ≤ ⌈(max_v l(v) + 0.5 · degreeL2Norm(Gᶜ)) / 2⌉`
where `l(v) = indepNeighbors G v`.
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture100

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 100](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj100)
(status O):

For a simple connected graph `G`,
`α(G) ≤ ⌈(max_v l(v) + 0.5 · degreeL2Norm(Gᶜ)) / 2⌉`
where `α(G) = G.indepNum` is the independence number,
`max_v l(v)` is the maximum over all vertices of the independence number of
the neighbourhood (in `G`), and `degreeL2Norm(Gᶜ)` is the square root of the
sum of the squares of the degrees in the complement `Gᶜ`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture100 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    let maxL := (Finset.univ.image (indepNeighborsCard G)).max' (by simp)
    (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ ⌈((maxL : ℝ) + (1 / 2) * (degreeL2Norm Gᶜ : ℝ)) / 2⌉ := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The independence number is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ G.indepNum := Nat.zero_le _

/-- The Euclidean norm of the degree sequence is nonnegative. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : 0 ≤ degreeL2Norm G :=
  Real.sqrt_nonneg _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture100

findings.description: The inherited `[Nontrivial α]` restricts the conjecture to graphs with at least two vertices, although source #100 says only “simple connected graph.” This is not a harmless omitted case: K₁ is connected, has independence number 1, maximum local independence 0, and complement degree norm 0, so the source's literal inequality becomes 1 ≤ 0. I proved this boundary counterexample in Lean. Excluding K₁ is a plausible intended correction, so I am flagging the domain choice as questionable rather than a definite mistranscription. I found no blanket singleton exclusion in the accessible source material; notably, the same source explicitly says “on more than one vertex” in #40.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII all.html, entry 100: “If G is a simple connected graph, then α(G) ≤ CEIL[(maximum of λ(v) + 0.5*length(Ḡ))/2]”; its only accompanying remark is the date April 21, 2004. Entry 40 explicitly includes “on more than one vertex.” Read at https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161800id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html. Definitions 4, 5, and 44 in wowIIdefs.js give the quantities used in the singleton calculation.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve and document the intended vertex domain. If the source includes K₁, replacing `[Nontrivial α]` with `[Nonempty α]` reproduces its literal assertion, which has the singleton counterexample; retain the existing statement only as an explicitly restricted/corrected version. If WOWII tacitly excludes K₁, supply that convention as justification for the existing hypothesis.

sources_consulted: https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161800id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html — entry 100, its surrounding remarks, and graph-size wording elsewhere on the page.
https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/ — cited collection's frameset and source links.

https://web.archive.org/web/20040626062038id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu:80/faculty/delavinae/gpc/graffitipc.pdf — E. DeLaVina, Graffiti.pc: A Variant of Graffiti, author preprint; especially §§2.2 and 3, including the definition of graph length on page 6.
FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Independence.lean and Degrees.lean at the reviewed commit — definitions and computable independence-number equivalence.
review.notes: Apart from the domain question, the formula matches the source: complement, local independence maximum, degree-sequence norm, both factors of 1/2, inequality direction, and ceiling are correct. Both anonymous sanity checks are faithful. Scratch checks compile successfully; the singleton counterexample and K₂ case use no sorry axioms. An independent exact-arithmetic enumeration found no failures among all connected graphs on 2–7 vertices. The accessible source records #100 as O, matching `research open`; live-source HTTPS timed out, so source verification used archived copies. All experiments are under /workspace/review/, and the reviewed file was not changed.
